newsitem.title: UK: UK NATURAL GAS SLIDES AS BUYERS STAND BACK.
newsitem.headline: UK NATURAL GAS SLIDES AS BUYERS STAND BACK.

text.p: UK natural gas prices were weaker on Thursday, especially for winter months, after buyers backed away from a falling market, traders said.
"The offers went down to yesterday's bid levels and then most of the bids started to evaporate," said one trader.

Balance of August traded at 9.55 pence a therm (p/th) at Theddlethorpe. September traded three times at 9.4 p/th, below Wednesday's lowest traded level, although Theddlethorpe gas commanded a 0.1 p/th premium.
October slipped to trade at 11 p/th, while the fourth quarter of this year changed hands three times at 13.3 p/th.
The first quarter 1998 was heard traded weaker at 17.125 p/th and ended the day at 17.00/17.10 p/th. The second quarter shed 0.1 p/th to trade at 11.35 p/th.
"It's weaker right the way across, but the summer is holding up a bit better," said one trader.

The trend on the over-the-counter market matched that on IPE futures which eased back with trade spread evenly across the forward months. A total of 435 lots changed hands in another fairly brisk day.
The trading time on the IPE gas contract will be extended by three hours starting on Friday, with no midday break.
